newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher Wednesday, with activity in the financial services sector sparked by the merger of Dean Witter, Discover & Co and Morgan Stanley Group Inc.
Analysts said markets would be buoyed by a higher long bond, a stronger dollar and a positive reaction to President Clinton's State of the Union address last night.
"What we'll expect is a good feeling in the market, and that should lead us to a higher opening," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
However, investors will be keeping an eye on the Federal Open Market Committee meeting for news on interest rates. The FOMC's two-day meeting ends today.
Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said the Morgan Stanley-Dean Witter merger should boost trading activity as "Wall Street starts covering Wall Street."
The merger will create a financial giant with a market capitalization of $21 billion.
Markets are likely to be buoyed by Clinton's address. The speech stressed improving the U.S. educational system and reaching an agreement with Republicans on balancing the federal budget.

"The State of the Union address was basically well received and the Republican response went over well," Cardillo said. He predicted a 10- to 15-point opening rise in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
The government releases December factory orders at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. Economists' consensus estimate is for a 0.8 percent drop, after a 0.4 percent decline in November.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average closed down 128.36 points, or 0.70 percent, at 18,185.97 after rebounding off lows.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was up 21.1 points at 4282.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Cisco Systems Inc stood at 66, down from a New York close of 67-1/8, after reporting second quarter earnings of $0.49 a share, a penny below the First Call consensus estimate.
The dollar firmed to a four-year high against the yen in Europe and gained on the mark. The dollar was at 123.15/23 yen, just off its high of 123.35, and 1.6477/82 marks.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was off 1/32 to yield 6.71 percent, and the Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 1.05 to 794.75.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column discussed investors' cool response to the initial public offerings of CarMax Group KMX.N and Vail Resorts Inc.

The New York Times' Market Place column said the question facing investors in Van Kampen American Capital Growth fund is not just whether shares will be available, but whether the fund can stay ahead of the pack once it loses its special "incubation" status. ((-- Wall Street Desk, 212 859-1730))
